/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 27 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2603 (-25)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3702 (-24)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2021 (-54)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1883 (-5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1020 (0)
CAPESIZE
The BCI 182 5TC lost $220 to settle at $33,575 today, with both basins losing ground. The Brazil/West Africa market remained subdued ahead of publication, although a C3 fixture for a post-index laycan window was reported at $35.00 after the index was published. In the North Atlantic, the market awaited further clarity on the latest spread, with some fronthaul enquiries in play. In the Pacific, the West Australia to China market was fixing at broadly similar levels to yesterday, following the high volume of fixtures concluded in the region yesterday. Operators were reportedly fixing at around the $14.00 level, while a miner was linked to several fixtures at sub-$14.00 levels. Nevertheless, the C5 route recorded a marginal gain of one cent to $13.945.

Atlantic
Cargill was rumoured to have fixed the Elka Vassilios (181,480 2011) for 170,000/10 Tubarao to Qingdao 26 November/2 December $35.00.

Asia
Rio Tinto took vessels for 170,000/10 Dampier to Qingdao 10/12 November at $13.80. Berge Bulk was linked to taking the Hebei King (181,299 2010) for 170,000/10 West Australia to Qingdao 12/14 November at $14.00. Last night, Vale took a vessel for 180,000/10 TRMT to Dung Quat 6/8 November at $8 or in the very low $8s region. LSS fixed their 150,000/10 Samarinda to Mundra 7/13 November at $10.75.
PANAMAX
Reports suggested the market remained firmly on the defensive today, with further losses recorded across both basins as the imbalance between available tonnage and cargo demand continued to weigh on sentiment. In the Atlantic, trans-Atlantic activity was said to remain subdued, with limited fresh enquiry and a growing number of vessels competing for the business available. Brokers reported that mineral requirements provided some activity, although rates continued to come under pressure, while grain demand offered little additional support as the bid-offer spread widened. Fronthaul conditions were similarly challenging, particularly from EC South America, where sources highlighted an increasing number of ballasters arriving from the Indian Ocean, adding further pressure to an already oversupplied market. Market talk suggested that charterers remained in a favourable position, with little incentive to improve their ideas as owners continued to adjust expectations in an effort to secure employment. The Pacific also lost further ground, with continued weakness in the North Pacific and Indonesia weighing on overall sentiment. Although EC Australia continued to provide some underlying demand, this proved insufficient to absorb the growing availability of tonnage, with rates across the region coming under renewed pressure. The P5TC consequently declined by $479 to close at $18,193.
SUPRAMAX
Another relatively subdued day with most reported trades and rumours actually concluded last week. The 11TC average was down $59 today to settle at $23,806, with most routes returning negative values. Sources said the Mediterranean and Continent markets look fairly balanced, after a clear out last week, but fresh November enquiry is needed to maintain the status quo. The US Gulf and EC South America are both softening as Charterers hold off where possible, with some Owners indicating a willingness to accept below last done. The PM Hayabusa (58,065 2013) prompt in the US Gulf was said to have fixed a trip to NC South Ameria in the $19,000's with WBC. Asia meanwhile continues with positive sentiment, however rate increases have now slowed, appearing to plateau despite supply still looking tight for the time being. The Jin Xing (55,496 2007) Singapore 28 October went on subjects for a trip via Indonesia to CJK at $17,000 with CCX and the Alasia (61,311 2014) open Navlakhi was placed on subjects by Team Bulk basis delivery Kandla for a trip Chittagong intention aggregates at $17,000.
HANDYSIZE
Building on the previous day’s tone, the market saw another relatively subdued session, with limited activity reported across most regions. The BHSI held unchanged at 1,020, while the 7TC average eased by $1 to settle at $18,362. In the Continent and Mediterranean, conditions remained soft, with limited visible activity and little fresh enquiry keeping rates under pressure. Across the South Atlantic and US Gulf, changes were minimal and the market appeared broadly balanced, with rates holding around last-done levels as fundamentals showed little sign of a notable shift. In Asia, however, pockets of activity emerged, supported by tight prompt tonnage and a steady flow of cargoes. A 34,000-dwt vessel open in the Red Sea was heard to have failed for a trip to the West Mediterranean with fertilisers at $12,750, although further details were not disclosed. The Silver (37,399 2023) open Callao around 5 November was fixed by Enesel for a trip via Chile to Australia with concentrates at around $20,000. The Szare Szeregi (39,072 2017) open Callao on 1 November was also fixed by Enesel for two laden legs to the Far East at around $21,000. Elsewhere, a 39,000-dwt vessel open in South Korea was placed on subjects for a trip to the west coast of Central America in the $19,000s. Further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
China Blast Furnace Activity

In the week to 23 October, Chinese blast furnace capacity utilisation fell 0.5 percentage points to 87.2%, while daily molten iron output remained near flat at 2.3 Mt/day during the period, MySteel data show. Out of the 247 sampled mills, 11.3% are in profit, a 3-percentage point increase from the prior week and the highest share since early-September.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape recovered throughout the session, with Nov and Dec leading the move higher as activity picked up significantly across the front months. Nov opened at 34,500 before dipping to 34,000, then rallied to 36,000, with heavy volume around 35,500–36,000, last trading at 36,100. Dec strengthened from 34,600 to 36,500, with main late activity at the highs. Q1 27 traded between 27,700–28,250, recovering strongly into the close to 28,500, while Q2 27 traded around 33,100–33,400. Cal 27 improved from 31,300 to 31,600 before easing slightly to 31,550.
